source.title: Feature-Robustness, Flatness and Generalization Error for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Henning Petzka; Michael Kamp; Linara Adilova; C. Sminchisescu; Mario Boley

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether flatness measures track the generalization gap using a new relative-flatness measure and comparisons with other measures; it does not reproduce Jiang et al.'s magnitude-aware perturbation measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own synthetic experiments and a LeNet5 experiment. Results cited from prior work are not rows. Hyperparameter values used to obtain local minima are setup details, not separate results.
record.test_reason: The study tests a related flatness–generalization hypothesis using weight-weighted Hessian curvature. It does not establish results for V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance before training error rises. Its PAC-Bayes comparator is not identified sufficiently in the supplied text to establish that it measures V7's specific quantity.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report stronger relative-flatness correlations than the tested alternatives on CIFAR-10 and derive a conditional connection requiring representative data and feature representations with approximately locally constant labels.
record.recipe_differences: Uses relative flatness, a layer- and neuron-aware Hessian measure, and studies its correlation with the gap; the version describes magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance. The paper's CIFAR10 experiment varies initialization, learning rate, batch size, and optimizer to obtain local minima.
record.method_sensitivity: Correlation depends on local label constancy in the synthetic experiment and on the selected feature layer. Layer-wise reparameterization changes correlations for non-invariant measures but not relative flatness.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 110 converged LeNet5 models on CIFAR-10, relative Hessian flatness reportedly correlates more strongly with generalization gaps than the tested Hessian, Fisher-Rao, PAC-Bayes and weight-norm alternatives.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-weighted Hessian curvature can predict generalization gaps among converged networks of one convolutional architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative flatness and Fisher-Rao remain invariant under tested layer rescalings; other measures' correlations decline. Relative-flatness correlation remains high but decreases at another fully connected layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization-measure correlations can depend on parameterization and feature-layer choice.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic relative-flatness correlations increase with class separation and disappear when labels lack local constancy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative Hessian flatness predicts generalization conditionally on local label constancy and representative feature-space data.

record.problems: Correlation values are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The CIFAR10 comparison aggregates 110 local minima from varying training setups; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The synthetic experiment uses a constructed distribution and feature extractor.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure-only correlations are retained as figure-only rather than assigning unreadable numeric values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Large-batch held-out performance penalties under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.

Correlation of magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance with generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The supplied text does not establish that the PAC-Bayes comparator implements this specific measure.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All cannot_determine states refer to the named claim versions; they do not negate the study's reported relative-flatness findings. Optimizer and batch-size variation generate local minima but are not reported as controlled tests of V4 or V5. Numerical correlation coefficients cannot be recovered from the supplied figure-free text.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Optimizer results are not reported as comparisons of held-out performance by optimizer.
No batch-size comparison of held-out performance.

Does not measure magnitude-scaled weight perturbations or compare against the specific measures in Jiang et al.; no SVHN results. It tests relative flatness and other measures on CIFAR10, and tests label-locality conditions synthetically.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.stage_stated: trained until convergence (loss less than 0.1 during an epoch)
rows.operation_detail: Measured relative flatness and generalization gap across 110 local minima obtained from different learning setups.
rows.measure: Correlation between relative flatness and generalization gap; authors state it is higher than for all competing measures analyzed.
rows.locator: Section 6; Figure 5 (also Figure 6 in Appendix C.1)
rows.note: The paper gives no numeric correlation values in the text. The aggregate covers 110 local minima.
rows.check: The reported strong correlation concerns relative Hessian flatness, not V7's specified perturbation-tolerance measure. It therefore cannot establish V7's effect.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.stage_stated: trained until convergence (loss less than 0.1 during an epoch)
rows.operation_detail: Measured trace of the loss Hessian, Fisher-Rao norm, PAC-Bayes flatness measure, and weight norm against the generalization gap.
rows.measure: Correlation of each listed measure with generalization gap; authors state relative flatness has higher correlation than each.
rows.locator: Section 6; Figure 5 (also Figure 6 in Appendix C.1)
rows.note: Distinct comparison measures are shown in the figure, but the text does not provide their separate numeric values.
rows.check: This bundles four distinct comparator measures and should be split. Their lower correlations than relative flatness do not establish incomplete effects: individual coefficients are unavailable, and the PAC-Bayes measure is insufficiently specified to link it to V7.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.stage_stated: trained until convergence (loss less than 0.1 during an epoch)
rows.operation_detail: Reparameterized trained networks by layer-wise factors and measured the resulting measure-to-gap correlations.
rows.measure: Correlation with generalization gap after reparameterization; relative flatness is invariant, while correlation for other measures declines substantially.
rows.baseline: correlations before reparameterization; exact values not stated
rows.note: Fisher-Rao is also stated to be invariant; this row records the relative-flatness result and the stated decline for other measures.
rows.check: This bundles invariant relative flatness and Fisher-Rao results with declining correlations for other measures. These are distinct outcomes, and none establishes what happens to V7's specified magnitude-scaled tolerance.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.stage_stated: trained until convergence (loss less than 0.1 during an epoch)
rows.operation_detail: Measured relative-flatness correlation with generalization gap at a fully connected layer other than the penultimate layer.
rows.measure: Correlation between relative flatness and generalization gap; authors report it remains high but is smaller than for the penultimate layer.
rows.baseline: penultimate-layer correlation; exact values not stated
rows.note: The text does not give numeric correlations or identify the other layer by name.
rows.check: The layer-dependent correlation concerns relative Hessian flatness. A smaller but still high correlation does not demonstrate a partial effect for V7.

rows.subject: synthetic 5-layer MLP (4-layer MLP feature extractor plus linear classifier)
rows.stage_stated: trained linear classifier by ridge regression; random MLP feature extractor
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation between relative flatness and generalization gap as synthetic class separation varied.

conditions.value: synthetic binary classification in feature space

rows.measure: Correlation between relative flatness and generalization gap; authors state it increases with local label constancy and disappears when labels are not locally constant.
rows.note: The text describes the direction and endpoint qualitatively but provides no numeric correlations.
rows.check: The experiment concerns relative Hessian flatness in synthetic ridge classifiers with random feature extractors. It does not measure V7's specified quantity. Correlation present with separated classes and absent without local label constancy should also be recorded separately.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
